definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.188) 'An item whose minimum permitted length is zero and whose length at execution time is zero' and §2023:3.177 'element of data whose minimum permitted length is zero and whose length at runtime is zero' are the same. §2002:8.5.4 item 4 lists this case explicitly (a variable-length logical record of zero characters). The scope does not change.

pending-clause.answer: 8.5.4 (2002) is the list that contains exactly this record (item 4), so the rule's term is defined in 2002 as GR16 uses it; the 2023 additions to that list are other kinds of item. 8.5.3 (types) names nothing GR16 uses. The witnessed space fill comes from the implicit MOVE, §2002:14.8.24.3 GR1 ('If identifier-1 is a zero-length item, it is as if literal-1 were specified as the figurative constant SPACE'), and §2002:14.5.8 rule 5 (space fill to the right). That is the behaviour shown by pb721_zero_length_record_2002 and the four-edition Theory, so the evidence holds at 2002.
